intro: The Prophet ﷺ as leader; Shahadah and Salah (1.7, 3.1, 3.2): the big ideas, key words and examples on one sheet. Keep it in your book and use it to revise (cover, write, check).

panels.title: Big questions
points: What does a new community need first: laws, leaders or shared beliefs? What did the Prophet ﷺ build in Madinah?
Can a peace treaty that looks like a loss turn out to be a great victory? How?
Should a leader always be obeyed? Where is the line?
Why might a few words, said sincerely, change the whole of a person's life?

panels.title: Islamic foundation
panels.text: Allah says: 'It is not for a believing man or woman, when Allah and His Messenger have decided a matter, to have any choice' (al-Ahzab 33:36).

keywords.def: the path of Islamic law and guidance from Allah
the Charter of Madinah: agreement between the groups of the city
the treaty with the Quraysh, 6 AH
9 AH, when tribes came to accept Islam
People of the Book: Jews and Christians
the declaration of faith: bearing witness
the call to prayer, which contains the Shahadah
the five daily prayers, the second pillar

panels.title: 1.7 The Prophet ﷺ as leader: establishing the Shari'ah in Madinah
points: Masjid an-Nabawi at the centre
Brotherhood of Muhajirun and Ansar
The Charter of Madinah between the groups
Command words: describe, explain, assess

panels.title: 1.7 Consolidation and expansion: treaties, conquest and the Year of Delegations
points: Hudaybiyyah: terms seemed harsh
Peace allowed people to meet Muslims freely
48:1: 'We have given you a clear conquest'
Invited kings to Islam peacefully

panels.title: 1.7 Opponents, prisoners and other communities; the hadith on obeying those in authority
points: Charter of Madinah with the Jewish tribes
Delegation of Christians from Najran
Abyssinia's Christian king protected Muslims
Obey leaders in what is right (ma'ruf)

panels.title: 3.1 The Shahadah: nature, role and use in Muslim life (Qur'an 3:18-19)
points: Ash-hadu an la ilaha illa Allah
Wa ash-hadu anna Muhammadan rasulullah
I bear witness ... and I bear witness ...
Vote in the Teams poll

panels.title: 3.2 Salah: nature, significance and importance
points: The second pillar of Islam
Five set prayers: Fajr, Dhuhr, Asr, Maghrib, Isha
Given directly in the Mi'raj
Discipline: punctual, organised days

panels.title: 3.2 How Salah is performed: wudu, times and qiblah
points: Face the Ka'bah in Makkah (2:144)
From the UK, roughly south-east
One direction unites the ummah
Vote in the Teams poll

panels.title: 3.2 Salah at home, in the mosque and at Jummah (Qur'an 62:9-11); exemptions
points: Home: anywhere clean; sunnah prayers loved at home
Mosque: congregation, 27 times the reward
Imam leads; lines straight; follow the imam
Replaces Dhuhr: khutbah then two rak'ahs

panels.title: 1.7 12-mark practice: treatment of opponents and prisoners
points: 'The Prophet's ﷺ treatment of opponents and prisoners was the main reason Islam spread.'
Assess this statement (12 marks)
Agree, disagree, conclude
Make a judgement

panels.title: 3.1 12-mark practice: 'Saying the Shahadah is the most important act for a Muslim'
points: 'Saying the Shahadah is the most important act for a Muslim.'
Assess this statement (12 marks)
Plan for, against, conclusion
Vote in the Teams poll

panels.title: A developed 'for' paragraph
points: Point: mercy to opponents drew people to Islam
Evidence: Thumamah was released and accepted Islam (Bukhari and Muslim)
Explain: kindness to an enemy showed Islam's truth
Link: so treatment of opponents helped Islam spread
Answer: One developed paragraph

panels.title: Using 3:18-19 in an answer
points: Quote briefly: 'Allah witnesses that there is no deity except Him'
Explain: Muslims join Allah's own witness
Apply: so the Shahadah is the foundation
Link to the statement
Answer: The passage supports the 'for' side
